transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well… I guess the main thing is I’ve been losing more time than I’d like to admit checking things, or sort of re-checking them. Like I’ll reread an email or a text over and over, or reopen folders on my computer, and before I leave the house or start work I’ll replay conversations in my head.

It’s not that I think I’m being unreasonable exactly… I mean, I’m just trying to make sure I haven’t made some serious mistake. But it’s been taking up chunks of time, and I’m starting to feel like maybe I need some help with it, if that makes sense.
Do you ever feel the need to check things to prevent something bad from happening?

Yes… I think that’s probably what it is. I don’t know if I’d say I’m expecting some disaster, exactly, but I get this feeling that if I don’t check, I might have missed something important or made some serious mistake.

So I’ll re-read an email or a text more times than I need to, or open the same folder again to make sure I didn’t put something in the wrong place. And before I leave the house or start work, I’ll sort of replay conversations in my head, trying to reassure myself I didn’t say something wrong. It’s a little embarrassing to say, but that’s the pattern.
Do you feel like you have to perform these checks or replays in a specific way or a certain number of times?

Not really a set number, no… at least I don’t think so. It’s more like I keep doing it until it feels like I’ve proven to myself I didn’t mess something up.

So with emails or texts, I’ll re-read them a few times, and with folders I’ll reopen them just to be sure. And the conversation replaying is kind of the same—I go over it in my head before I leave or start work, just trying to make sure I didn’t say something wrong. I know that probably sounds excessive, but it’s not like a ritual exactly… more like I’m trying to get that “okay, it’s fine” feeling.
Do you feel like these checks or replays are necessary to prevent something bad or harmful from happening to yourself or others?

I suppose… yes, in a way. I don’t usually think of it as stopping someone from getting hurt, exactly, but it feels necessary to prevent something bad coming from a mistake I made.

Like with emails or texts, I keep re-reading them because I’m worried I missed something or said it wrong. Or I’ll reopen folders to make sure I didn’t put something where it shouldn’t be. And before I leave the house or start work, I’ll replay conversations in my head, just to prove to myself I didn’t say something that could cause a problem.

I know that may sound a bit much… but that’s the feeling behind it, I think.
Do you feel like your checking is more about avoiding mistakes or making sure everything is perfect?

I think it’s more about avoiding mistakes than making everything perfect… though maybe those overlap a little.

It’s not like I need things to be beautiful or exactly arranged. It’s more that I get worried I’ve missed something important—like I sent an email with the wrong wording, or put a file in the wrong folder, or said something in a conversation that could cause trouble. So I end up re-reading emails and texts, reopening folders, replaying conversations in my head before I leave or start work.

I know it probably sounds like overdoing it, but it feels like I’m trying to prove to myself I didn’t make some serious mistake.
Do you ever feel like you need to check things because they don't feel 'right' or aren't arranged in a way that feels symmetrical or balanced to you?

Not really in terms of symmetry or things being arranged just so, no. I mean, I like things organized, but that’s not what brings me in.

It’s more that I lose these chunks of time re-reading emails or texts, reopening folders, or replaying conversations in my head before I leave the house or start work. It’s like I’m trying to prove to myself I didn’t make some serious mistake. I hope that makes sense.
Do you feel like you're trying to control the outcome of a situation when you're checking things over and over?

Maybe a little, yes… though I don’t think of it as controlling things exactly. It’s more like I’m trying to make sure I haven’t caused a problem by missing something.

When I keep re-reading an email or a text, or reopening a folder, or replaying a conversation in my head before I leave or start work, it’s like I’m trying to prove to myself I didn’t make some serious mistake. I know that probably sounds excessive, but in the moment it feels hard to move on until I’ve checked.
Do you think you would still feel the need to check things if someone else verified that everything was correct?

I think it would help, probably… at least for a little while. If someone I trusted said, “Yes, that email is fine,” I’d feel better.

But I’m not totally sure it would stop it every time. I might still have this nagging feeling that I should look again myself, like maybe I missed something or maybe they didn’t notice the thing I’m worried about. That’s kind of the pattern—I lose time re-reading emails or texts, opening folders again, replaying conversations in my head before I leave or start work, just trying to reassure myself I didn’t make some serious mistake.

I know that may sound like I’m not trusting people, and I don’t mean it that way. It’s more like I have trouble letting it go unless I’ve checked it myself.
Do you think your checking would stop if you were absolutely certain that you hadn't made a mistake, or is there something else that drives you to continue checking?

I think if I were absolutely certain, then… yes, I’d like to believe I could stop. That’s what I’m trying to get to, really.

But the problem is I don’t seem to feel certain enough. Even after I’ve checked, there’s still this little doubt that maybe I missed something important. So I end up re-reading the email again, or looking back at a text, or opening the same folder one more time. Sometimes I’ll replay a conversation in my head before I leave the house or before I start work, just to make sure I didn’t say something wrong or overlook something serious.

I know that probably sounds like more than normal double-checking. I’m not trying to be difficult—I just get stuck trying to prove to myself that I haven’t made some major mistake.
Do you think you would feel the need to check something again if you knew you had done it correctly, but it wasn't done in the best possible way?

Yes… I think so, unfortunately. I mean, I’d probably tell myself, “It’s correct, it’s fine,” but then I can get caught on whether I wrote it the best way, or whether there’s some detail I could have missed.

That’s kind of why I came in, honestly. I keep losing these chunks of time re-reading emails and texts, reopening folders, and going back over conversations in my head before I leave the house or start work. It’s not that I want everything to be perfect exactly… or maybe I’m trying to say that in a better way. It’s more like I’m trying to reassure myself that I didn’t make some serious mistake.

I know that probably sounds excessive. I’m not trying to waste time with it. I just have a hard time moving on sometimes, even when part of me knows it was probably okay.
Do you think you would still check things repeatedly if you knew you had done them correctly, but not necessarily to the highest standard?

Yes, I think I probably would… maybe not every single time, but more than I’d like to admit.

If I know something is technically correct, I can still get stuck on whether I missed something or whether it could cause a problem somehow. That’s really part of why I came in. I keep losing chunks of time re-reading emails and texts, reopening folders, and sort of replaying conversations in my head before I leave the house or start work.

I’m not trying to be overly picky, or difficult. It feels more like I’m trying to prove to myself that I didn’t make some serious mistake. Does that make sense?
Do you think your checking behavior would decrease if you were able to accept that some mistakes are inevitable and not catastrophic?

I think it probably would help, yes. If I could really accept that a mistake wouldn’t be the end of the world, I imagine I wouldn’t feel so driven to keep checking.

Right now, though, I get stuck there. I came in because I keep losing these chunks of time re-reading emails and texts, reopening folders, and mentally replaying conversations before I leave the house or start work. It’s like I’m trying to prove to myself I didn’t make some serious mistake.

I know that may sound a bit excessive… I’m trying to be honest about it. I think if I could tolerate the possibility of being imperfect without treating it like a disaster, I’d be able to move on more easily.
Do you think you would consider a task complete if it was done correctly, but not perfectly?

I’d like to say yes, that if it’s correct then I can just call it done. And sometimes I can.

But honestly… a lot of the time, not really. I’ll know an email or a text is basically fine, or that I already checked a folder, but I still end up going back over it. I lose time re-reading things, reopening files, and replaying conversations in my head before I leave the house or start work.

It’s not that I’m trying to make everything perfect, exactly. It’s more like I’m trying to reassure myself that I didn’t make some serious mistake. I know that may sound a bit much, but that’s what seems to happen.
Do you think you would feel satisfied with a task if it was done correctly, but not to your personal standards of quality?

I think… not completely, no. I mean, if it’s done correctly, I can tell myself that should be enough, and I don’t want to make it sound like I’m impossible to satisfy.

But I came in because I keep losing chunks of time going back over things — re-reading emails and texts, reopening folders, replaying conversations in my head before I leave the house or start work. It’s like I’m trying to prove to myself I didn’t make some serious mistake.

So even if it’s technically correct, if it doesn’t feel up to my own standard, I don’t always feel settled. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do you think your need to check things repeatedly is more about avoiding mistakes or achieving perfection?

I think it’s more about avoiding mistakes, honestly. Or at least that’s how it feels to me.

I don’t sit there thinking, “This has to be perfect.” It’s more that I’ll re-read an email or a text, or reopen a folder, because I’m worried I missed something important or did something wrong. And then I can lose a lot of time with it, including replaying conversations in my head before I leave the house or start work.

I know that probably sounds excessive… but it’s like I’m trying to prove to myself that I didn’t make some serious mistake. Does that make sense?
Do you think you would still check things repeatedly if you were certain that you had met the minimum requirements for a task, even if you didn't think it was perfect?

I think… yes, probably. I wish I could say that meeting the minimum requirements would be enough, because logically I know it should be.

But I still find myself going back over things — re-reading emails or texts, reopening folders — even when I basically know it’s been done. It’s not always about making it perfect. It’s more like I’m trying to get that feeling of certainty that I didn’t overlook something serious.

And I know I’ve mentioned this already, but I lose chunks of time with it, including mentally replaying conversations before I leave the house or start work. I don’t mean to sound dramatic… it’s just that “good enough” doesn’t always feel safe enough, I guess.
Do you think you would still feel the need to check things repeatedly if someone told you that your work was good enough, even if it wasn't perfect?

Yes… I think I probably would, even if someone told me it was good enough.

I’d want to accept that, and part of me would feel reassured. But then I’d still get this pull to check again — like re-reading the email or text one more time, or reopening a folder just to make sure I didn’t miss something. It’s not that I’m trying to be difficult or make everything perfect. It’s more like I’m trying to prove to myself I didn’t make some serious mistake.

And I know that can sound a bit much, but it’s been taking up real chunks of time, especially before I leave the house or start work, because I’ll mentally replay conversations too. Does that answer what you’re asking?
Do you think you would still feel anxious or compelled to check if you knew you had made a small mistake, but it wasn't catastrophic?

I think… yes, even if it was a small mistake and not catastrophic, I’d probably still feel pulled to check.

I know that might sound like I’m overreacting, and I’m not trying to make it bigger than it is. But once I notice there could’ve been a mistake, I start wanting to go back over it — re-read the email or text, reopen the folder, that kind of thing — just to prove to myself I didn’t miss something more serious.

It’s less about the actual small mistake, maybe, and more about the uncertainty that comes after it. Does that make sense?
Do you think your checking behavior is more about preventing harm or ensuring everything is flawless?

I think it’s more about preventing some kind of mistake from slipping through than making everything flawless.

I mean, I don’t need every email or text to be beautifully written or perfect, exactly. It’s more that I’ll re-read it, or reopen a folder, because I’m trying to convince myself I didn’t miss something serious. Same with replaying conversations in my head before I leave the house or start work.

I know that probably still sounds excessive, but it feels like I’m trying to make sure I haven’t caused a problem, not just polishing things for the sake of it. Is that the kind of distinction you mean?
Do you think you would still feel the need to check things repeatedly if you knew you had done them correctly, but someone else might still find a mistake?

Yes… I think I still would, honestly. Even if I felt pretty sure I’d done it correctly, the idea that someone else might spot something I missed would still kind of get to me.

It’s not that I want everything to be perfect, exactly. I know that probably sounds like splitting hairs. But I’ll lose these chunks of time re-reading emails or texts, reopening folders, going back over things, because I’m trying to prove to myself there isn’t some serious mistake in there.

And sometimes I’ll mentally replay conversations too, especially before I leave the house or before I start work. I know it may not look like a huge thing from the outside, but it does take up time. Is that the sort of thing you mean?
